A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DASHA and Auto-AR study. Their main text, figures, tables, algorithms, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and added content.

before.justification: V1 reports original supervised-model experiments, satellite-model fine-tuning, architecture-search analyses, and Time-LLM reproduction results in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds satellite comparisons, subsampling experiments, computational-cost measurements, and zero-shot Auto-AR evaluations.

M1.justification: DASHA and standard Auto-AR remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1 and Appendix B. Appendix F adds a zero-shot adaptation that segments the test history into rolling-window samples, fits Auto-AR on those samples, and restricts lookbacks to {64, 96, 128, 192}.

E1.justification: The datasets and classification/forecasting targets are retained. Appendix F adds a matched history-only forecasting scenario for Auto-AR; v1 compared fully trained baselines against zero-shot FMs and explicitly identified zero-shot evaluation as unstudied. The 20% subsampling changes data quantities rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 expands the satellite comparison from six to eleven pretrained models by adding DOFA-Base, DOFA-Large, Satlas, ScaleMAE, and Clay. These are reported comparisons, including previously cited but unevaluated models. Table 14 also removes the reported TEMPO and TimesFM comparison entries for ILI.

E3.justification: V2 adds 20%-training-data evaluations with random sampling for genomics/satellite data and trailing-series sampling for forecasting, history-only Auto-AR evaluation, MAE reporting, and GPU-time accounting. These substantially extend the evaluation design. The original training settings in Appendix B remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test sensitivity to reduced training data, compare computational costs, and examine how zero-shot competitiveness deteriorates with forecasting horizon (Appendices D-F). The existing fifteen-seed architecture-clustering analysis and satellite channel-exclusion analysis are retained.

E5.justification: The fifteen-seed architecture analysis and initialization-seed search range are retained. V2 introduces no new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practice; its added benchmark results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds satellite scores, MAE results, timings, subsampling outcomes, and zero-shot Auto-AR results. In Table 2, DASHA remains at 77.85, while newly included DOFA-Large scores 78.80; DASHA's average rank changes from 3.33 to 6.06 under the expanded comparator set. Main genomics and forecasting aggregates are retained, while TEMPO/TimesFM ILI scores become unknown entries.

T1.justification: The AR equation and existing mathematical description are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and the new rolling-window Auto-AR adaptation introduces no substantive formal analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claim that specialized FMs struggle against tuned supervised baselines and the contributions of DASHA and Auto-AR. Added evaluations support and qualify this thesis without materially redefining the headline contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 5.2 argues for benchmarks addressing actual FM use cases. V2 removes the unstudied-zero-shot limitation and explains that FMs gain an advantage at longer horizons, potentially through pretraining. It also expands efficiency interpretation and qualifies satellite competitiveness in light of DOFA's stronger results.

D1.justification: V2 discloses L40/L40S hardware, runtime-accounting rules including estimated tuning costs, subsampling procedures, and zero-shot lookback settings. Existing ASHA settings, training epochs, preprocessing instructions, and code-access URLs remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands discussion of earlier satellite-model evaluations, including Xiong and Corley, while Section 4.3 explains TOTEM's exclusion. References also add Clay, Cheng, and several specialized-model papers and remove Zhou and Troyanskaya (2015). The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 tightens prose, converts several numbered related-work and baseline/results subsections into inline headings, reorganizes forecasting discussion, and adds appendices D-F. It also updates the publication header and an affiliation. The overall narrative and much of the original wording are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds four figures and six tables, revises Figure 1's satellite panel, and reformats the main comparison tables. Existing PCA and closed-source comparison plots become Figures 5 and 7. Satellite Tables 12 and 13 exchange numbering and placement, preserving their underlying content.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evaluation through stronger satellite comparators, a matched zero-shot baseline, data-scarcity tests, and quantitative computational costs. These address v1's acknowledged zero-shot gap and largely qualitative efficiency argument. Reporting problems temper the gain: Figure 3 says only one satellite FM beats DASHA at 20% data, whereas Table 19 shows two, and parts of the new MAE tables repeat corresponding MSE entries. These issues weaken some added reporting, but the broader comparisons and explicit horizon-dependent limitations provide a substantial net improvement.
